subject: if-st-dy
title: IF.ST.DY.-----SOC.RT.
description: Diagram in SD(SY)-27 (Spectacle-Diversion Syndrome, Level One) accompanying Braxton's distinction between style-driven and substance-driven cultural movements: 'the most basic factor that determines the particulars of spectacle-diversion initiations has to do with the style of a given movement — rather than its intention.' (C)IF-ST-DY (information-style dynamics) is crossed with SOC-RT (social reality): the question is what information-style-dynamics produces when crossed with social-reality, given that style functions as the basic factor of spectacle-diversion. VT-PLT (vibrational platform) and ACT (activism) form the upper bridge between subject and partner. (R)TM (reality of time) anchors a temporal frame for SOC-RT. INFO-DY (information dynamics) feeds in from the upper-left. AFN (affinity) and APP-RDEF (apparent redefinition) cluster on the upper-right output. ACC-DY (accelerated dynamics), POL-DY (political dynamics), and PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) form the central-lower chain. (P)AGT (point-of-activation agent) anchors the lower-center as a trigger node. Structural argument: information-style-dynamics becomes productive of social-reality through a doubled mediation — vibrational-platform with activism above, accelerated-dynamics with political-dynamics below. The (p) prefix on agent registers Braxton's diagnostic that activism here is *triggered* rather than *sustained*: the diagram exposes that what looks like substance is really point-of-activation manipulation, with style-dynamics as the deeper driver of apparent social-reality.
